transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-01
Time: 4:00 PM PDT
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Sophie Park (Redwood AE), Mateo Ruiz (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (CSM), Dr. Rachel Lin (CTO, Newbridge), Marcus Hale (IT Ops), Priya Singh (Security), Daniel Ortiz (Product)

Summary: Kickoff to align on onboarding plan, security reqs, sandbox provisioning, and next steps.

[00:00] Sophie Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, we'll do a quick intros then jump into the onboarding plan. I'm Sophie, I'm the AE on this account and Aisha will be your CSM, and Mateo our SE.
[00:18] Dr. Rachel Lin: Hi all, Rachel here. We're excited to get started. Marcus will be our sysops lead and Priya handles security.
[00:26] Marcus Hale: Hey, thanks. Appreciate you folks making time.
[00:30] Aisha Khan: Quick agenda – high-level timeline, security/compliance items, sandbox Dedicated provisioning, network checklist, and then we capture action items. Sound good?
[00:40] Daniel Ortiz: Yep that's good. We're trying to move relatively fast, aim for a pilot in June if possible.
[01:05] Sophie Park: Great – pilot timeline is doable; typical onboarding is 2–4 weeks for a sandbox pilot depending on network approvals. We'll share a detailed plan. Mateo, do you want to cover the Dedicated vs hosted notes?
[01:18] Mateo Ruiz: Sure. So for Newbridge we're recommending Redwood Dedicated sandbox to start – gives you reserved capacity and isolation for PHI-sensitive flows. Hosted is fine for lower-risk data, but Dedicated lets you control model pinning, and easier to do per-token tracing for cost analysis. Note – our naming is sometimes Redwood Dedicated or Redwood Private for on-prem variants, folks mix those up, sorry for that.
[01:48] Dr. Rachel Lin: For us data residency and audit controls are very important – we need SOC 2 evidence and SSO/SAML integration. Also KMS for key management ideally.
[02:05] Aisha Khan: Absolutely. We'll send our SOC 2 report and an SSO/SAML checklist. We support SAML 2.0 and enterprise SSO providers. For KMS we can integrate with AWS KMS or customer-managed HSM in Private deployments. For Dedicated we can do KMS integration as well.
[02:25] Priya Singh: On KMS, is the key exchange managed by you or do we keep control? We need to ensure keys never leave our control where possible.
[02:35] Mateo Ruiz: For Dedicated we can support BYOK patterns – you keep the keys in your KMS and we reference them. For Private on-prem we can map to your HSM. I'll follow up with a tech note.
[02:48] Marcus Hale: For network, we'll need a list of IPs and egress domains to allow. Also do you support VPN peering or direct connect?
[02:58] Mateo Ruiz: Yes, VPN peering and VPC peering are supported for Private and Dedicated. For the hosted API we provide TLS endpoints but IP allowlist is available through our enterprise console. We'll share an allowlist doc.
[03:18] Daniel Ortiz: How do you handle logs/audit trails? We need audit logs for requests and RBAC for developers.
[03:26] Aisha Khan: You get request-level logs, model and token breakdowns via Redwood Console. RBAC and SSO tie into permissions, and we can set retention policies for logs. For PHI we recommend stricter retention and we can discuss exporting logs to your SIEM via our webhook.
[03:44] Dr. Rachel Lin: Great. On the pilot success criteria: latency under 300ms on the average 512-token prompt, throughput ~20 QPS during peak tests, and we want no data exfil risks.
[03:58] Mateo Ruiz: We'll capture that. Performance depends on model choice and quantization; for low latency we might suggest a trimmed model variant. We'll run benchmarks in your sandbox Dedicated cluster.
[04:15] Sophie Park: Can you give us brief infrastructure constraints? Daniel?
[04:20] Daniel Ortiz: Our infra team can provide a subnet and VPN. We have a proxy with TLS inspection which sometimes breaks streaming. We need to know requirements for streaming responses.
[04:34] Mateo Ruiz: If there's TLS inspection it can disrupt streaming. We can do chunked transfer fallback (non-stream) for initial tests; for full streaming we recommend bypassing MITM proxy for those endpoints or using a tunneled connection. We'll document the ports and headers.
[04:50] Marcus Hale: Noted. We'll try to get a bypass for the sandbox.
[05:00] Sophie Park: Next, onboarding timeline – we propose: Day 0: kickoff (today). Day 1–3: security docs and SSO config. Day 4–8: network tests and sandbox provisioning. Week 2: ingest sample prompts and run performance benchmarks. Week 3: iterate on model choice and validate telemetry. Week 4: evaluate pilot and decide production plan. Does that align?
[05:25] Dr. Rachel Lin: That timeline looks fine if we can get approvals this week.
[05:32] Priya Singh: On security docs, besides SOC 2 we'd like encryption in transit and at rest details and data retention policy. Also any subcontractors involved?
[05:44] Aisha Khan: Yes we'll include data encryption and subprocessor list. For Dedicated/Private, data flow is contained to your cluster and we provide audit logs. Subprocessors are listed in our compliance package.
[05:58] Daniel Ortiz: About cost – what's the delta between starting pilot on hosted vs Dedicated?
[06:05] Sophie Park: Hosted is lower commitment but can have higher per-token variability. Dedicated has monthly reserved cost but predictable unit economics. For a short pilot, we often do a short Dedicated sandbox (pro-rated) to get accurate performance and cost telemetry. We'll follow up with a cost estimate.
[06:22] Dr. Rachel Lin: For our procurement, we'll need a letter of intent and scope to get internal sign-off. Can you share a simple pilot SOW?
[06:31] Sophie Park: Yes – we'll send a one-page pilot SOW with goals, timeline, and deliverables.
[06:38] Mateo Ruiz: Technical note on sample prompts – to emulate production we recommend a mix of 70% short prompts (<=128 tokens) and 30% long (around 512 tokens) to capture KV cache behavior. Also include expected concurrency.
[06:55] Daniel Ortiz: We'll put that in a spreadsheet and share.
[07:00] [crosstalk] Marcus Hale: Also any specifics on network MTU or websocket keepalive we should tune?
[07:06] Mateo Ruiz: We'll include a network checklist – keepalive and websocket timeouts, allowed ports, and guidance for TLS inspection.
[07:16] Sophie Park: Any other blockers we should know about?
[07:19] Priya Singh: One more – remote code execution risk with plugins/tools. We don't plan to use external tool calls in pilot; want them disabled by default.
[07:29] Aisha Khan: By default tool-calling is off. We'll ensure it's disabled for your sandbox.
[07:35] Dr. Rachel Lin: Perfect.
[07:40] Mateo Ruiz: I'll also include a short note on quantization and model variants – quantized variants can reduce cost while maintaining accuracy for certain workloads, but we should test on your prompts.
[07:52] Daniel Ortiz: Who will be our primary support contact during pilot?
[07:56] Aisha Khan: I'll be your CSM day-to-day. Mateo is the SE for technical support and Sophie handles contract and escalation.
[08:05] Sophie Park: Ok let's recap and finish with next steps.
[08:12] Sophie Park: Action items – Aisha will send SOC 2 and SSO checklist by Thursday. Mateo will schedule the deep network test and share allowlist instructions. Daniel will share the sample prompts and expected QPS. Marcus will provide network/VPN details. Redwood to provision sandbox Dedicated and share access details.
[08:35] Dr. Rachel Lin: Sounds great, thanks everyone.
[08:40] Aisha Khan: We'll follow up with the onboarding plan doc and calendar invites for the deep-dive.
[08:46] Sophie Park: Thanks all – meeting adjourned.

Notes on transcript quality: Some proper nouns may be mis-transcribed (e.g., 'Redwood Dedicated' sometimes referred to as 'Redwood Private'), timestamps are approximate. Shared artifacts referenced: onboarding-plan.docx (link to be shared), sso-checklist.xlsx, sample-prompts.csv (customer to provide).

End of transcript.
